steps.name: QC, normalization and variance-stabilized matrix
steps.question: After filtering low-count genes from the 12000 x 120 Salmon gene-count matrix (counts.csv) and normalizing library size across the 60 case / 60 control whole-blood samples (metadata.csv), what does the variance-stabilized expression matrix and sample-level QC (library size, detected genes, PCA of technical metrics) look like, and are there outlier samples or technical drivers that could confound subgroup detection?

grounding.reason: No knowledge_recommend tool attached in this session; standard DESeq2-style filter/normalize/VST is dataset-appropriate for a 12000x120 raw Salmon count matrix but not tied to a retrieved procedure.

acceptance_criteria: Genes with near-zero counts across all 120 samples are filtered with a stated, reproducible threshold (e.g., min counts in >=X samples)
Library-size normalization and a variance-stabilizing transform (DESeq2 vst or equivalent) are applied and the resulting matrix is saved for downstream clustering
Per-sample QC metrics (library size, number of detected genes) are reported and any outlier samples are flagged with a stated rule, not silently dropped
A PCA on the normalized matrix is produced and PC1/PC2 are checked for correlation with library size or other technical metrics to flag potential confounding of any downstream clustering

steps.name: Multi-method unsupervised clustering on top variable genes
steps.question: On the top variable genes of the normalized 120-sample whole-blood matrix, do hierarchical clustering, k-means, and PCA-plus-Gaussian-mixture / graph-based clustering (Louvain/Leiden on a k-NN graph) agree on a candidate number of subgroups (k=2..8), and how does any recovered clustering align with the known 60 case / 60 control label?

grounding.reason: No knowledge_recommend tool attached; multi-method clustering with ARI-vs-label cross-tab is a standard unsupervised QC step for this design.

acceptance_criteria: Feature selection to the top N most variable genes (N stated explicitly, e.g. top 2000 of 12000) is performed on the VST matrix from T1S1

At least two independent unsupervised methods (e.g. hierarchical clustering with Ward linkage, k-means, and a graph-based Louvain/Leiden clustering on a k-NN graph) are run across a range of k from 2 to 8
For each method/k, cluster assignments are cross-tabulated against the case/control label (metadata.csv) to quantify overlap (e.g. adjusted Rand index) versus independent structure
Candidate k values agreed upon by multiple methods are reported explicitly, not just a single method's output

steps.name: Consensus clustering and stability assessment
steps.question: Using consensus clustering with bootstrap resampling (subsampling of the 120 samples across many iterations) on the top-variable-gene matrix, what is the most stable number of subgroups (by consensus CDF / proportion-of-ambiguous-clustering, PAC) and how reproducible is each sample's cluster assignment?

grounding.reason: Consensus clustering with PAC/CDF stability is the standard method to answer 'how many subgroups and how stable' for a bulk expression cohort; no retrieved procedure available in this session.

acceptance_criteria: Consensus clustering (e.g. ConsensusClusterPlus-style resampling, >=100 iterations, subsampling ~80% of samples per iteration) is run for k=2..8 on the same feature set used in T1S2
A stability metric (consensus CDF area under curve, PAC score, or equivalent) is reported per k and used to justify the selected optimal k(s), not chosen by eye alone
Per-sample cluster stability (e.g. average consensus with assigned cluster) is reported so that samples with ambiguous/unstable assignment are identified
The final recommended number of subgroups (or a statement that no subgroup structure beyond case/control is stable) is stated explicitly with the supporting stability values

steps.name: Characterize subgroups: differential expression and label association
steps.question: For the stable subgroup assignment selected in T1S3, which genes are differentially expressed between subgroups (using the raw count matrix with DESeq2), and does subgroup membership associate with the case/control label beyond chance (chi-square/Fisher test) or cut across it independently?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 contrast on discovered subgroups plus categorical association test; no retrieved procedure available.

acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 differential expression is run on raw counts (counts.csv) with the stable subgroup assignment from T1S3 as the primary factor, using Wald tests with BH-adjusted p-values
A contingency table of subgroup membership x case/control label is tested (chi-square or Fisher's exact test) and the association strength (e.g. Cramer's V) is reported
Top differentially expressed genes (padj < 0.05) distinguishing subgroups are output as a ranked table for downstream pathway interpretation
The report states plainly whether subgroups are driven by case/control status, independent of it, or a mix, based on the contingency analysis

steps.name: Pathway enrichment for subgroup-defining genes
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among the genes differentiating the stable subgroups identified in T1S4, and do these pathways suggest a coherent biological axis (e.g. immune activation, cell-cycle) underlying the subgrouping?

grounding.reason: Standard pathway enrichment step using the human WikiPathways reference confirmed present in the environment.

acceptance_criteria: Over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment is run using the ranked/significant gene list from T1S4 against the human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols) found under the reference store
Gene identifiers in the DE results are matched to HGNC symbols used by the WikiPathways gmt (using the human UniProt ID mapping reference if Ensembl/Entrez conversion is needed)
Enriched pathways are reported with adjusted p-values (BH) and effect direction relative to subgroups
If no pathway reaches significance, this null result is reported explicitly rather than showing only nominal top hits as if significant

plan.title: Unsupervised subgroup discovery in 120-sample blood cohort
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 121 columns incl. gene id, 120 whole-blood samples, 60 case/60 control, unpaired, single batch). The research question asks whether structure exists beyond the case/control label. This requires: (1) standard count QC/normalization to remove technical variance that could masquerade as subgroups, (2) unsupervised clustering with multiple algorithms/resolutions on the normalized, most-variable genes, (3) formal stability assessment (consensus clustering / bootstrap resampling) to determine the number of robust subgroups rather than picking a k by eye, and (4) a check of whether discovered subgroups align with or cut across the known case/control label and any measurable technical covariates, plus a biological characterization of what distinguishes them. Because the metadata only records condition (120 x 2), no other covariates are available to adjust for, so batch/technical confounding must be assessed from the expression data itself (e.g., library size, PC loadings) rather than assumed absent. All steps operate on the bulk count matrix or its derived gene-level results, so bulk-transcriptomics, statistical-modeling, and enrichment agents are used; no single-cell, spatial, or other specialized modality is present.
